cim_eredeti: IBA Legal Agenda 2026: artificial intelligence leads seven priorities confronting lawyers amid technological disruption and global rule of law pressures
szoveg_eredeti:
The International Bar Association (IBA) has published its Legal Agenda 2026, which identifies artificial intelligence (AI) as the most pressing issue facing lawyers around the world, as technological advances reshape legal service delivery, talent development, pricing, client relationships and expectations and access to justice.

The 2026 edition marks a departure from the 2025 Agenda, which ranked the rule of law as the legal profession’s foremost concern, with AI in second place in the list of seven priorities. The latest Agenda reflects the accelerating influence of AI across the legal sector and the urgent need for lawyers, law firms, regulators and professional associations to respond to its opportunities and challenges.

Claudio Visco, IBA President, commented: ‘The 2026 update to the IBA Legal Agenda reflects the fact that the adoption and development of artificial intelligence is fast becoming the most impactful technological advancement of our time. It is already transforming how legal services are delivered, how lawyers develop their expertise and how clients expect to be served. The challenge before us is to embrace innovation without compromising the independence, professional standards and ethical responsibilities that underpin the practice of law. Lawyers have a crucial role to play in helping to regulate and promote proper governance of AI. As the global voice of the legal profession, the IBA aims to become a reference point and key player in this arena, including through our newly founded IBA Artificial Intelligence Institute, launched in June 2026. The decisions we make now will shape the future of our profession and its contribution to society for generations to come.’

Jaime Carey, IBA Immediate Past-President, remarked: ‘That AI has overtaken the rule of law as the profession’s leading priority should not be interpreted as diminishing the fundamental importance of the rule of law. Rather, it demonstrates the scale of the transformation facing lawyers worldwide. At a time of technological disruption, geopolitical uncertainty and growing pressure on democratic institutions, the legal profession must remain a steadfast defender of justice, professional independence and the rights of individuals. The IBA has a vital role in bringing the global legal community together to meet these challenges. The future may be uncertain, but what is clear is the IBA’s commitment to navigating these changes as an international community.’

A strategic roadmap for the global legal profession

Launched in 2023 by former IBA President Almudena Arpón de Mendívil Aldama, the IBA Legal Agenda forms part of the Association’s five-year strategic focus for 2023-2028.

Building on consultations held in New York and London with leaders of major international and national law firms, the Agenda is updated annually to identify the most critical issues facing the legal profession with the aim of promoting practical solutions to the challenges.

The 2026 IBA Legal Agenda highlights a profession undergoing profound transformation. As a global organisation representing the legal community internationally, the IBA is uniquely positioned to unite and guide the legal community to address these challenges.

Over the next year, the priorities outlined in this Agenda will serve as the foundation for the IBA’s strategic initiatives and partnerships. Consultations will continue in 2027 to inform the next edition.
